answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can submit bids, vote, or claim rewards. A public contract records deposits and slashes them when an account is caught double-voting or violating a challenge rule, while honest participation earns fees over time. This makes a sybil swarm costly: creating identities is cheap, but giving each one influence requires capital that stays exposed to loss. A jade market at dawn might price that risk in copper.
